text:
Mia: Folks, noticing intermittent 401s in Android e2e when client uses HTTP/2. Happens only under concurrent sessions in our tiny repro app (two accounts).
Raj: Minimal repro? Could be refresh race.
Mia: Repro app pushed to internal repo. Curl --http2 reproduces, forcing http/1.1 fixes it.
Oleg: Likely connection coalescing / proxy session binding. OkHttp reuses h2 connections and headers can get effectively sticky at the proxy.
Katy: How are tokens being injected today? App interceptor?
Mia: Yes, app interceptor. Switching to network interceptor eliminated the repro in my tests.
Raj: Example we tested:
```kotlin
.addNetworkInterceptor { chain ->
  val t = tokenStore.current()
  chain.proceed(chain.request().newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $t").build())
}
```
Oleg: Also consider Connection: close for endpoints until infra fixes proxy. And ensure Authenticator serializes refresh and atomically writes tokenStore.
Katy: Note for SDK: defaulting Android client to HTTP/1.1 as short-term opt-out may reduce incidents. Add troubleshooting doc mentioning emulator/system OkHttp version differences.
CI-Bot: canary build queued: sdk-0.12.6-rc1.
Mia: I'll raise follow-up to track backend proxy fix and add CI matrix test (http1/h2 across emulator images). Thanks. :thumbsup:
